title: High School In Hell City
content: I call it Hell City because I haven't discovered it's name yet. I'm a kid again, somewhere between late middle schooler and high schooler, and I'm alone. The city is spaced out, but busy and dirty and it's looking more ran down every day. Moving cross over a bridge that overpasses a flood channel, usually dry but it wasn't this time. I'm on the city bus that runs past the school. The kids are alway mean, but in a fake nice way. For example, who accidentally adds a huge scoop of non-edible purple glitter onto my rather piddly lunch tray anyhow? I hate them, and the feeling is mutual. The bell rings and I need to grab a bathroom break before getting on the bus. And I know I gotta be quick about it. It's no school bus, it WILL leave without me, and it feels like 20 miles from my house in the dream, so I don't mess around. I'm a guy in the dream, so like any guy I run to the boys room with white tile walls and small cherry blossom pink tile floors. I get to a urinal as more boys file in. All of a sudden I'm crowded in as more guys shove their peckers into the urinal I'M ALREADY USING. HELLO?! GROSS. Like, literally who fucking does that, but everyone is too preoccupied with getting business done to care. Again that entitled, smarmy attitude fills the entire bathroom as I writhe free from these jerks who swarm the stalls, urinals, and sinks. Washing hands is a no go, so I leave the restroom, and race towards the intersection and I see the bus. The bus that is boarding. And leaving. Without me. And I'm pissed. But it's done and the walk home begins. I'm making good time when I come across the bridge again. I see a few kids from school on it, but to be clear, it is not for pedestrians, it's for cars and cars alone. there's no space for anyone to walk, and only the flimsiest ledge made of what looked like plastic or powder coated metal to stand on, on either edge of it. I yet at them. Feeling more like my adult self again, I tell them to get down from the edge where they're walking, and that it's dangerous. They look back at me and sneer. "It's our only way across, not every one is like you!" They yell back. I dunno what to say to that. In the moment, I know they're right. It's not like I have a car either, I am walking too, but I try to understand how I was different. I took my chances walking on the bridge as close to the sides as possible, but no cars come so I managed to get to the otherside just fine. I make it into Sinister Suburbia. Less dense, more meticulously upkept, and on the way to my ACTUAL neighborhood. Sinister Suburbia is where my previous middle school was. The PRISTINE Jasket Preparatory. It boasted light gray buildings, and neon pink piping, and it was filled with duplicitous weasels and backstabbing friends. I walked past it with nothing but relief that I was finally out of it and into a new school in my mind. A shitty school, but not THAT hitler youth factory. The neighborhood is pretty in the early afternoon sun, it's warm enough but a cool breeze hits me and sends chills over me. I'm in my hoodie I always wear, and I pull it tighter around me as I loop around the neighborhood and finally make it to my own. It's kind of ugly, and it's modeled after the one I grew up in. Run down, but in a lived in and comfortable kind of way. I finally make it to my door and go to pull out my keys. My. Keys. "FUCK, I DID NOT JUST LEAVE MY KEYS AT SCHOOL. " and that's when I woke up. at 5. AM. Fucking. Mallworld. Dreams.
